title: Atomium
blurb: The Atomium in Brussels, built for the 1958 World's Fair, in simplified schematic form: nine 18 m stainless-steel spheres arranged as an iron crystal unit cell magnified 165 billion times, joined by twenty tubes and rising 102 m over the Heysel Plateau.

systems.name: Nine spheres
systems.description: Nine 18 m stainless-steel-clad spheres arranged as an iron crystal unit cell magnified 165 billion times.

systems.name: Cladding, windows and lighting
systems.description: The stainless-steel cladding panels, window bands, panoramic band and LED meridian lighting of the spheres.

systems.name: Tubes
systems.description: The twenty 3 m tubes joining the spheres: twelve along the cube edges and eight from the vertices to the center.

systems.name: Supports and foundations
systems.description: The three support tripods under the lower spheres, added after wind-tunnel tests, with base pads and the foundation raft.

systems.name: Interior circulation
systems.description: The lift, escalators, stairs and the bottom sphere exhibition floor.

systems.name: Top sphere restaurant
systems.description: The panoramic restaurant inside the top sphere, with room for about 140 guests.

systems.name: Entrance pavilion
systems.description: The reception pavilion with its boomerang-shaped roof, entrance stairs and esplanade.

explanations.nine spheres: The nine stainless-steel-clad spheres, each 18 m in diameter, arranged as an iron crystal unit cell magnified 165 billion times: eight cube vertices plus the body center. Sphere positions on the cube frame are schematic.
explanations.cladding panels: The schematic stainless-steel cladding panels of the nine spheres. The spheres were originally clad in aluminium; the faded aluminium sheets were replaced with stainless steel during the 2004 to 2006 renovation.
explanations.window bands: The rings of windows around the equators of the eight non-top spheres. Exact window arrangement is schematic.
explanations.top sphere panoramic band: The band of panoramic windows around the top sphere, with views over Brussels. Exact glazing is schematic.
explanations.led meridian lights: The LED lighting integrated into the meridians of the spheres, installed during the 2004 to 2006 renovation. The lights can flash along each meridian, symbolising the range of an electron around its core. Exact layout is schematic.
explanations.upper edge tubes: The three tubes along the upper cube edges, 3 m in diameter, joining the top sphere to the three upper outer spheres. Exact interior arrangement is schematic.
explanations.ring edge tubes: The six tubes along the middle cube edges, 3 m in diameter, joining the upper and lower outer spheres. Exact interior arrangement is schematic.
explanations.lower edge tubes: The three tubes along the lower cube edges, 3 m in diameter, joining the bottom sphere to the three lower outer spheres and enclosing stairs. Exact interior arrangement is schematic.
explanations.diagonal tubes: The six oblique tubes from the outer vertices to the central sphere, 3 m in diameter, enclosing escalators. Exact interior arrangement is schematic.
explanations.central elevator tube: The two vertical diagonal tubes forming the central spine of the building, from the bottom sphere through the center to the top sphere, carrying the lift. Exact interior arrangement is schematic.
explanations.tube collars: Schematic joint collars where the tube sections meet at mid-span.
explanations.support tripod 1: One of three support tripods under the lower outer spheres. The original design had no supports under the lower spheres, but wind-tunnel tests showed an 80 km/h wind would have toppled the structure, so support columns were added. Exact tripod geometry is schematic.
explanations.support tripod 2: One of three support tripods under the lower outer spheres. The original design had no supports under the lower spheres, but wind-tunnel tests showed an 80 km/h wind would have toppled the structure, so support columns were added. Exact tripod geometry is schematic.
explanations.support tripod 3: One of three support tripods under the lower outer spheres. The original design had no supports under the lower spheres, but wind-tunnel tests showed an 80 km/h wind would have toppled the structure, so support columns were added. Exact tripod geometry is schematic.
explanations.tripod base pads: The schematic foundation pads spreading the three tripods into the ground.
explanations.foundation raft: The schematic foundation raft under the whole structure.
explanations.elevator shaft: The lift shaft in the central vertical tube, running from the bottom sphere to the top sphere. Exact shaft form is schematic.
explanations.elevator car: The lift car for 22 people. It climbs at 5 m/s and reaches the top sphere in 23 seconds; in 1958 it was the fastest lift in Europe. Exact car design is schematic.
explanations.escalators: The escalators in the oblique tubes; the longest measures 35 m, among the longest escalators in Europe. Exact placement is schematic.
explanations.stairs: Schematic stair runs inside the lower edge tubes.
explanations.bottom sphere exhibition floor: The floor of the bottom sphere, reserved for the permanent exhibition on the 1950s, Expo 58 and the construction of the Atomium. Exact layout is schematic.
explanations.restaurant floor: The restaurant floor inside the top sphere. Exact layout is schematic.
explanations.kitchen and bar core: The schematic kitchen and bar core of the top-sphere restaurant.
explanations.panorama deck: The schematic observation deck above the restaurant, with the panoramic view of Brussels.
explanations.reception pavilion: The new reception pavilion with its entrance canopy and ticket desks, built during the 2004 to 2006 renovation. Exact form is schematic.
explanations.boomerang roof: The boomerang-shaped roof of the reception pavilion, added in the 2004 to 2006 renovation. Exact shape is schematic.
explanations.entrance stairs: The schematic stairs from the pavilion level up to the bottom sphere.
explanations.esplanade: The concrete esplanade at the foot of the building, redeveloped during the 2004 to 2006 renovation with continuous benches. Exact layout is schematic.
